items.prompt: What does ∇f(x)=0 alone prove for a differentiable nonconvex interior problem?

options.why: Nonconvex stationary points need not minimize.

options.text: A feasible boundary optimum with known multipliers

options.why: A zero first derivative says nothing about that.

options.text: Only stationarity, not a global minimum
options.why: A maximum or saddle can also be stationary.

items.explanation: For example -x² has zero derivative at its maximum 0.
